title: Slinky waves: transverse and longitudinal
examples: What is the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: Coils squash and stretch along the slinky

explain.say: Grab a slinky spring, the bouncy toy coil. Stretch it out on the floor with a friend. You can send a wave along it in two very different ways. Both carry energy from one end to the other, but the coils move differently. Let us try both.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Coils move up and down, across the slinky

explain.say: First, flick your end side to side. Look at the board: the coils move up and down, across the direction the wave travels. That is a transverse wave. Transverse means across. Light and ripples on a pond are transverse. Which way do the coils move?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Coils move up and down, across the slinky

explain.say: Up and down, yes! Now push and pull your end, along the slinky. Look: bunches of squashed coils, then stretched-out gaps, travel along. Squashed parts are compressions; stretched parts are rarefactions. This is a longitudinal wave, meaning along. Can you see the bunches?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Coils squash and stretch along the slinky

explain.say: Great! Sound is a longitudinal wave: air squashes and stretches as it passes. And here is the big idea: the slinky itself does not travel to your friend. Each coil just wobbles back and forth. Only the energy moves along. Does the slinky move across the room?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Coils squash and stretch along the slinky

explain.say: No, only the energy travels. You have nailed it! Look at the two cards side by side. Wow fact: earthquakes send both kinds of waves, and longitudinal P waves arrive first, so scientists in Japan use them to send warnings seconds before the shaking. Try the slinky at home!

faq.a: In a transverse wave, the particles move at right angles to the direction the wave travels, like up and down while the wave moves along.
In a longitudinal wave, the particles move back and forth along the same direction the wave travels, making compressions and rarefactions.
Compressions are regions where particles are squashed together. Rarefactions are regions where they are spread apart.
Sound is longitudinal. Air particles squash and stretch along the direction the sound travels.

faq.q: Does a wave carry the material along with it?
faq.a: No. Waves transfer energy, not matter. Each particle just wobbles about its own place.

facts: Sound waves are longitudinal; light and other electromagnetic waves are transverse.
Earthquake P waves are longitudinal and travel faster than transverse S waves.

quiz.say: In a longitudinal wave, the particles move…
quiz.show: In a longitudinal wave, the particles move…
quiz.why: Longitudinal means along: particles move back and forth parallel to the wave.

wrong.2: Circular motion is seen in water surface waves, not longitudinal waves.

quiz.say: Which of these is a transverse wave?
quiz.show: Which of these is a transverse wave?
quiz.why: Light is an electromagnetic wave, and all of these are transverse.
